definitions.meaning: to disband a group is to split it so its members go their separate ways
in Britain a school is said to close for the holidays at the end of term, when pupils are released

explanation.surface: A teacher's urge to scatter the class and get the holidays going.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are phrasal: a band can split for good, and British pupils finish term and go home on the last day.

definitions.meaning: ..., a pet form of Polly, is a traditional name for a pet bird that talks
an old word for the top of the skull, still seen in ... tax, a tax per head

explanation.surface: A remark about a pet bird's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Pet talking birds were traditionally called Poll, and the old word for the skull survives in counting heads at an election.

definitions.meaning: to write something with a pen, as in writing a letter
shut in an enclosure, as sheep or cattle are kept in a fold

explanation.surface: An author or prisoner who kept writing while locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense comes from the writing tool, the other from the fenced enclosure for animals.

definitions.meaning: crucial, of decisive importance
inclined to find fault and pass harsh judgement

explanation.surface: A claim that finding fault is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucial moment and a fault-finding review share the same adjective in two senses.

clue.text: Show support and respect to a lady

definitions.meaning: to defend or back someone publicly
the old courtesy of a man rising to his feet when a woman enters

explanation.surface: Advice on gentlemanly manners: back her up and be courteous.
explanation.definitionFit: Defending someone and rising from your seat out of courtesy are both described with the same phrasal verb.

annotationWithheld.why: Everyone retired after being stranded! (7): EACH (everyone) inside BED for BEACHED, but 'retired' must give BED and also signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
to rook someone is to cheat them out of money

explanation.surface: A big crowd of victims conned by a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent or dishonest, as in a corrupt official.

clue.text: Food a dieter may wish to waste

definitions.meaning: a piece of battered and deep-fried fruit, vegetable or meat
to squander time or money bit by bit, usually with away

explanation.surface: A fried treat that someone on a diet would rather throw out.
explanation.definitionFit: A battered deep-fried snack, and the verb meaning to squander gradually.

clue.text: Marxist takes pledges to make mutual concessions

parts.note: Com. is an abbreviation for Communist, a follower of Marx
solemn undertakings or vows

explanation.surface: A communist politician gives his word in order to reach a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both sides give ground to reach an agreement.

parts.note: a quarrel that ends a friendship, read either as the upset itself or literally as people dropping from favour

explanation.surface: A neutral description of what happens when family harmony breaks down.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel or rift is what follows when a relationship is disrupted.

definitions.meaning: to kiss and cuddle
cheek or impudence, as in the sheer brass of it

explanation.surface: An indignant reaction to someone getting fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing and cuddling, and also British slang for cheek or effrontery.

definitions.meaning: in racing, to draw level with or catch the leaders
told off or called to account for a fault

explanation.surface: Someone made progress only after being told off.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner catching the field and a person being rebuked share the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Sadly, I still rate him a pedant

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grudging admission of still admiring a fussy, rule-bound man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges the letters of I STILL RATE; 'him a' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sticks rigidly to the exact wording of rules is a stickler for detail.

clue.text: Was responsible for bounder being without employment

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for bounder wraps around the other piece

parts.note: an old-fashioned word for a cad, a dishonourable man
use, as in putting something to employment

explanation.surface: A rogue blamed for his own unemployment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is read in its old sense 'outside', not 'lacking', so the bounder surrounds the employment; the surface wants an out-of-work rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about something is to be its cause.

parts.note: staff are the people employed by an organisation
Life was a famous American picture magazine; the possessive gives 'of'

explanation.surface: Workers at a US magazine are hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's is read as 'of': the magazine's staff is the staff of Life.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional phrase for the basic food that sustains people, from the Bible.

definitions.meaning: gave way or came to nothing, as a failed business does
origami is Japanese paper folding, so the paper has been creased into shape

explanation.surface: Someone flopped exhausted after an afternoon of paper art.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that went under, and paper creased into a shape, take the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Henry and I transmit message from Canadian port

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
to send a document by facsimile over a phone line

explanation.surface: Two people send a message from a harbour in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Nova Scotia, a major Atlantic harbour city.

clue.text: Hedging or paling round the garden

definitions.meaning: being evasive and avoiding a direct answer
a barrier of stakes or boards enclosing a plot

explanation.surface: A choice between a hedge or a picket fence for the garden boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive sparring in argument, and a run of stakes or boards bounding a plot.

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters are in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A partner of a Thomas Hardy character with striking charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy is Oliver Hardy, of the comedy double act; his partner was Stan.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan, the thin half of the classic film comedy duo, partnered Oliver Hardy.

clue.text: Popular prior is given a canary

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
former means earlier or previous

explanation.surface: A well-liked monastery head is presented with a pet songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: Canary is US slang for someone who 'sings' to the police; the surface makes 'prior' a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A canary is slang for a police snitch, who 'sings'.

clue.text: Its scent may make fellow frown

definitions.text: Its scent may make fellow frown

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
to lower, rhyming with '...', is to scowl or look sullen

explanation.surface: A bloom whose perfume makes a man scowl, perhaps through hay fever.
explanation.walkthrough: Lower here is the verb meaning to scowl (also spelt lour), not 'make lower'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloom is what gives off scent, and the whole clue describes one causing a sneezing man to frown.

definitions.meaning: means to do something
determination or strength of purpose

explanation.surface: Someone means to show determination.
explanation.definitionFit: Determination, and the auxiliary of future intention.

clue.text: I talk to Tory with discretion and direct looks

indicators.note: talk means the word I is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the letter I said aloud sounds like the organ of sight
Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
tact is diplomatic discretion

explanation.surface: A speaker addresses a Conservative tactfully, looking him in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talk' signals the homophone: I spoken gives the word for the organ of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting someone's gaze directly.

clue.text: Little ones can be served in the bar

definitions.meaning: small children

definitions.text: can be served in the bar
definitions.meaning: small measures of spirits poured in a pub

explanation.surface: Children are allowed in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Toddlers, and small measures of whisky or rum.

parts.note: manipulative here means kneading muscles with the hands, not scheming

explanation.surface: A warning about a scheming man.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who gives massages works by manipulating muscles.

clue.text: It began badly and ended in defeat

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters have gone wrong and need reordering

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A game that started poorly and finished in a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges IT BEGAN; 'and ended in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrashing is a heavy defeat.
